business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Portfolio organised into four stated pillars: Masstige/Value Retail, Ethnic Brands, Luxury Retail and Digital First Brands.
- Ethnic described as a "scalable platform spanning well-known & marquee premium and designer led brands" and "India's largest & most comprehensive ethnic wear portfolio", with 2200 Cr+ annual revenue and 670+ stores across brands; it spans apparel, beauty, accessories and jewelry.
- Galeries Lafayette positioned as "setting new benchmarks in luxury retail with a differentiated, first-of-its-kind department store in India", with strong brand and celebrity collaborations driving footfalls.
- One designer-led brand is framed as "establishing a global Indian luxury brand", delivering "another 100 Cr+ quarter in a weaker market vs LY"; another as "blending Indian heritage with contemporary luxury".
- Market backdrop the deck positions against: value retail faces "high competitive intensity" with more choice in lower-tier markets, and digital fashion brands are expanding omni-channel with D2C brands accelerating offline expansion.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Ethnic — TCNS drag] The deck gives two readings of ethnic growth side by side: "Ethnic grew 4% vs LY" and "Ex. TCNS growth at 14%", indicating TCNS is materially diluting the reported ethnic number.
- [Cost inflation] Input cost pressures are flagged as emerging, with "inflation visible across raw materials, logistics and wages" and "further escalation remains a key monitorable".
- [Demand disruption] Occasion-led demand moderated YoY because "Adhik Maas disrupted the peak wedding related consumption this quarter", while broader demand was in line with previous quarters.
- [Channel shift] Quick commerce is called out as "emerging as a new growth channel" in the market update.
- [Definition] The deck defines secondary revenue as "the amount paid by consumer net of taxes" — the digital portfolio's 16% secondary revenue growth is on that basis, not reported revenue, and both that figure and the 11% portfolio revenue growth exclude WROGN.

risks.note: Global economic uncertainty, inflationary pressures, elevated household indebtedness and fluctuations in consumer sentiment may impact discretionary spending; prolonged demand softness could affect sales growth, profitability and inventory productivity. Mitigation stated: presence across multiple consumer segments, categories and price points, disciplined cost management, agile planning, stronger inventory and working-capital management, sourcing flexibility and channel-mix optimisation. Structural concentration reinforcing this risk: exports are only 1.04% of total turnover and the sole international market named is the USA, so essentially all demand is Indian discretionary consumption (BRSR Section A, back-filled from the registry/governance bundles). The MD&A separately flags the West Asia conflict as the key near-term risk, through higher energy prices, freight costs and supply-chain disruptions.

Rapidly changing consumer preferences, evolving lifestyles and increasing digital influence continue to reshape fashion consumption; failure to anticipate these shifts could impact product relevance, customer engagement and market share. Mitigation: continuous investment in consumer insights, product innovation, category expansion and digital capabilities, and a balanced portfolio across consumer segments and occasions.

Increasing use of digital platforms, interconnected systems and consumer data heightens exposure to cybersecurity threats, data breaches and operational disruptions; a significant incident could impact business continuity, stakeholder trust and brand reputation. Mitigation: cybersecurity and resilience framework with security controls, continuous monitoring, disaster recovery and business continuity, employee awareness programmes, vulnerability assessments and governance reviews; information and cyber security systems were independently assessed by one of the Big 4 audit firms.

Increasing competition for premium retail locations may constrain access to high-quality spaces and result in higher occupancy costs, affecting expansion plans, store economics and profitability - directly material given 1,273 stores over 7.9 million sq ft and continued footprint addition. Mitigation: market presence and long-standing developer/landlord relationships, plus focus on store productivity, space utilisation and in-store experience to maximise returns.

Scaling across multiple verticals - design, retail, marketing, e-commerce and more - increases the need for skilled talent in a competitive Indian fashion retail sector. Mitigation: leadership development, succession planning, capability building, employee engagement, a strong employee value proposition, internal mobility, and access to the Aditya Birla Group's consumer-segment talent pool.
risks.risk: Talent attraction, retention and capability development

risks.note: The Indian fashion and lifestyle market is highly competitive across organised and unorganised domestic players, international brands, digital-first businesses and emerging D2C brands; increased competition may lead to pricing pressure, higher customer acquisition costs and market-share erosion. Mitigation: brand equity, product innovation, wider consumer reach, differentiated cross-channel experiences, a diversified portfolio and omni-channel presence.

Reliance on digital platforms, automation, analytics and artificial intelligence brings risks of technology obsolescence, integration complexity, implementation challenges and evolving regulatory expectations; failure to adopt emerging technologies may impact operational efficiency and competitiveness. Mitigation: scalable platforms, phased implementation, strong governance, and continued investment in digital capability, data quality, process integration and responsible AI adoption.

The growth strategy involves scaling multiple businesses, expanding the retail footprint, strengthening omni-channel capabilities, integrating new platforms and driving operational transformation; delays in execution, ineffective implementation of strategic initiatives or inability to realise expected benefits may impact growth, profitability and return on investment.
